ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended by Ley 19/2018 and Ley 6/2023; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo (Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010); Real Decreto 609/2023, de 11 de julio, establishing the Registro Central de Titularidades Reales (Central UBO Register); transposition of Directive (EU) 2018/843 and Directive (EU) 2021/2101.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of the non-resident parent/shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Register of companies in the jurisdiction of the parent entity (e.g., Companies Registry, Chamber of Commerce registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; if the issuing country is not party to the 1961 Hague Convention, consular legalization at the Spanish Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (poder notarial) granted by the foreign incorporators/shareholders to a Spanish attorney or agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary or foreign notary duly legalized; if granted abroad, apostilled and translated by an officially sworn translator (traductor jurado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the signatory state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution of the parent company's board approving the incorporation of the Spanish SL and appointing its directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary of the parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copies and NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) applications for the appointed directors and beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish consulate, Spanish National Police (NIE issuance), or passport authority of the holder's state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies and sworn translation; consular certification may be required where the 1961 Convention does not apply

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors and beneficial owners against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, SEPBLAC advisories, the OFAC SDN List (best practice for USD-denominated wire payments), and commercially available PEP registers. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs and high-risk geographies under Articles 14-17 of Ley 10/2010 and R.D. 304/2014, including source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and continuous transaction monitoring throughout the contract lifecycle.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) - https://www.rmc.es/ and CIRCE online portal (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas) - https://sociedades.economia.gob.es for streamlined SL incorporation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be expressed in Spanish characters and grammatically compatible; foreign-language names must be transliterated or orthographically adapted to Spanish. The name must not be identical or phonetically/semantically confusingly similar to any existing registered company, must not infringe private rights, and must comply with Spanish public order and legal-entity type designations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms falsely suggesting public or royal sponsorship: 'España', 'Estado', 'Gobierno', 'Ministerio', 'Administración', 'Comunidad Autónoma', 'Ayuntamiento', 'Diputación', 'Nacional', 'Oficial', 'General'
Terms reserved for other legal forms or requiring authorization: 'Sociedad Anónima', 'S.A.', 'Cooperativa', 'Comanditaria', 'Mutualidad', 'Agrupación de Interés Económico'

Financial-sector terms requiring prior ministerial authorization from Banco de España, CNMV or DGSFP: 'Banco', 'Caja', 'Seguros', 'Crédito', 'Sociedad de Valores', 'Fondo de Pensiones', 'Entidad de Pago'
Energy infrastructure-sensitive tokens: 'Red Eléctrica', 'Hidráulico' or any denomination implying official designation as grid operator without prior sectoral approval
Identical or confusingly similar denominations to already registered companies or to the official name of any public institution
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No statutory extension of the 90-day certificate is available; if the certification (certificación negativa de denominación) is rejected, the applicant may file a reconsideration request (recurso de reposición) with the Central Commercial Registry within one month, followed by an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Directorate General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith (DGSJFP). Judicial challenge would be brought as a recurso contencioso-administrativo before the competent administrative court in Madrid within two months. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a revised list of up to five preferred alternative names to the RMC for prioritized processing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditional: a virtual service office may support the initial registration and correspondence requirements, but under Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital, the registered office must coincide with the actual place of management or principal operations. For a 500-kV substation electrical contractor, public-sector clients, energy licensing authorities, and labor inspectors will expect a demonstrable physical presence in Spain; a purely virtual office would create a material permanent-establishment and licensing risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: approximately 70% probability of unannounced workplace safety or labor inspection (Inspección de Trabajo y Seguridad Social) during active 500-kV substation projects within the first 24 months, and 35-45% probability of a domiciliation verification visit if a third-party virtual office address is used at incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory official fee schedule approved by the Ministry of Justice for name certificates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (escritura de constitución) including statutes, no conflict-of-law and acknowledgment formalities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official notarial tariff (Arancel de los Notarios) scaled to registered capital and page count

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and legalization of parent company corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, good standing, board resolution)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority of the issuing country (e.g., Secretary of State / Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing government fee per document, assuming three original documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traducción jurada) into Spanish of parent company public documents and certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Settled Sworn Translator (traductor jurado) authorized by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 30-50 per certified page, estimated 12-15 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and certification of the Power of Attorney granted to the Spanish incorporator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Notary or the authorized official of the Spanish Consulate abroad

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) application and processing for each foreign director/UBO
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish National Police (Comisaría General de Extranjería) or Spanish Consulate

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Spanish Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 5, 20-23, 28, 30, 32, 33, 43, 62, 159-171, 210-212 and 225-232; supplemented by the Commercial Registry Regulations approved by Royal Decree 1784/1996 and Law 14/2013 on entrepreneurs and electronic incorporation procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, coordinated through the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central) for name clearance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), including the articles of association, followed by registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry and publication of the registration notice in the Official Gazette of the Commercial Registry (BORME).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully assumed and paid at incorporation. No statutory escrow account is required, and a bank certificate of deposit is generally unnecessary where the founders state in the deed that they assume liability for the reality of the contribution; a bank account and deposit evidence remain advisable for auditability and banking onboarding. Until capital reaches EUR 3,000, the statutory reserve regime and creditor-protection rules in Article 4 apply, including allocation of at least 20% of profit to legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000 and enhanced shareholder liability on liquidation in specified circumstances. Notarial, registry, name-certificate, publication and professional fees are variable and are not included in the stated zero national filing-fee figure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the Company shall subscribe and fully pay the shares allocated to each founder in accordance with the notarised deed and approved articles; (2) the registered office shall be established at [full Spanish address], with authority granted to update the address within the statutory limits; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or, where applicable, [names] are appointed as directors in the structure stated in the articles, each accepting office and declaring no legal impediment; (4) the appointed officer is authorised to obtain the tax identification number, open bank accounts, register the Company with relevant authorities, and execute documents necessary to commence lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its electronic name-certification service or an authorised notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-clearance request identifying up to five proposed names, preferably including the required corporate suffix Sociedad Limitada or S.L. Verify that the name is not confusingly similar to an existing registered name. Obtain the negative name certificate, which is generally valid for three months for execution of the deed and may be reserved for the applicable statutory period.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names in priority order
Founder power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Foreign founder documents, apostilled or legalised and accompanied by sworn Spanish translations where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an alternative name request. If the certificate contains an error, request correction from the Central Commercial Registry before execution of the deed. Challengeable registry decisions may be appealed through the commercial-registry review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare ownership, governance and registered-office documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Spanish notary public (notario) and, for foreign investors, the relevant Spanish consular, apostille and sworn-translation channels.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine the shareholding, capital allocation, management model, powers of representation, financial year and registered office. Obtain Spanish tax identification numbers for foreign shareholders, directors and beneficial owners where required. Execute powers of attorney before a Spanish notary or foreign notary and apostille or legalise them, with sworn Spanish translations where necessary.
required_dossiers: NIE or NIF documentation for non-Spanish persons
Registered-office title, lease, or occupancy authorisation
Corporate certificates and powers of attorney for entity shareholders
Evidence of capital contribution or founder liability declaration under the Capital Companies Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct incomplete identification, legalisation, translation or beneficial-ownership documents before the signing appointment. Obtain a fresh certificate or renewed power of attorney if a document expires or does not satisfy the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public authorised to execute deeds of incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the complete incorporation dossier and sign the public deed. The notary verifies founder capacity, identity, name certificate, articles, capital subscription and payment evidence or the statutory founder declaration. The deed must identify the shareholders, contributions, share numbers, management body, registered office and corporate purpose.
required_dossiers: Capital deposit certificate or statutory contribution declaration
Powers of attorney and corporate authorisations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve notarial objections by amending the articles, correcting identification or supplying missing evidence. If a founder cannot attend, provide a properly executed and legalised power of attorney accepted by the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification and file tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT), generally through Form 036 and the electronic tax portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the provisional NIF of the company, register the registered office and economic activities, and file any applicable exemption or notification concerning the tax on capital transactions. The deed and identification documents must be submitted in the form required by the AEAT. The company must update its NIF to permanent status after Commercial Registry registration.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney for the tax representative, if applicable
Foreign shareholder corporate documents and tax numbers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond electronically or through the assigned AEAT office to information requests, correct Form 036 inconsistencies and provide certified translations or legalisations. Replace the provisional NIF with the permanent NIF immediately after registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the company with the Provincial Commercial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the registered office, through the notary's electronic filing channel or direct authorised filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an authorised electronic copy of the incorporation deed, together with the required registry forms and proof of tax identification. The Registry reviews legality, articles, capital, management appointments, corporate purpose and registered office. After approval, obtain the registry certificate and confirm publication of the registration notice in BORME.
required_dossiers: Authorised electronic or certified copy of the public deed
Evidence of applicable tax filing or exemption
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a qualification notice, cure each stated defect within the applicable validity period, obtain a corrected deed if necessary, and resubmit. A negative qualification may be appealed to the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith or challenged before the competent court within statutory periods.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration corporate, municipal and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT, Spanish Social Security General Treasury (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social), relevant municipality, and the competent autonomous-community industrial authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the permanent NIF, update AEAT activity registrations, legalise accounting and corporate books electronically, register as an employer before hiring, and submit any municipal opening, works or activity declarations. Register the company as an industrial installation contractor where required and obtain sector-specific habilitation before performing regulated high-voltage work.
required_dossiers: Technical qualifications and responsible technician documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected electronic filings, respond to municipal or regional authority requests, and do not commence regulated installation work until the required habilitation, project approvals and commissioning authorisations are effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: The competent industrial and energy department of the autonomous community where the installation or project is located, applying Law 24/2013 on the Electricity Sector, Royal Decree 1955/2000, and Royal Decree 337/2014 approving the high-voltage technical regulation and its complementary technical instructions. The Directorate-General for Energy Policy and Mines of the Ministry for Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge may be competent for facilities within or exceeding state jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Administrative authorisation for the electricity installation, comprising prior administrative authorisation, administrative authorisation for construction and authorisation for operation or exploitation (autorización administrativa previa, autorización administrativa de construcción and autorización de explotación), together with registration in the applicable administrative register. The contractor must also satisfy the requirements for an authorised high-voltage installation company under Royal Decree 337/2014 and ITC-RAT 03.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental body of the relevant autonomous community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment; for state-jurisdiction projects, the Ministry for Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge, Directorate-General for Environmental Quality and Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Project-dependent. A high-voltage substation and associated lines require screening against Annexes I and II of Law 21/2013 and applicable regional legislation. A full environmental impact assessment is required where Annex I thresholds or protected-area criteria apply; otherwise simplified assessment, environmental screening, or no EIA may apply. The determination must be obtained before construction where legally required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with the Industrial Emissions and environmental permitting framework where applicable, Royal Decree 509/2007 and Royal Decree 553/2020 for hazardous-waste and waste-transfer requirements, Law 7/2022 on waste and contaminated soils, water-discharge authorisations under the Water Law and applicable river-basin rules, and regional noise and soil-contamination rules. Prevent transformer-oil releases through bunding and spill controls; manage PCB-contaminated equipment, SF6 and other greenhouse-gas-containing switchgear under applicable EU and Spanish rules; obtain separate discharge or waste permits where thresholds or activities require them.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before construction and energisation, obtain the applicable municipal works and activity approvals, fire-prevention compliance under the Building Technical Code and applicable autonomous-community fire rules, and certificates or inspections required by the municipality and industrial authority. Demonstrate structural design, foundations, seismic and wind loads, electrical clearances, earthing, fire compartments, oil containment and emergency access. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, Royal Decree 614/2001 on electrical-risk protection, Royal Decree 1627/1997 for construction works, coordination of contractors, worker training, lockout and high-voltage safety procedures, and mandatory commissioning inspections by an authorised control body where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), including the AEAT electronic headquarters (Sede electrónica de la AEAT). The relevant tax registration is administered through the census of entrepreneurs, professionals and withholding agents.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada must obtain a provisional Número de Identificación Fiscal (NIF) before or during incorporation and a definitive NIF after registration of the deed with the Commercial Registry. The application is generally submitted to the AEAT using Form 036, electronically where required, by the legal representative or an authorized tax adviser. The file normally includes the notarized incorporation deed, articles of association, Commercial Registry documentation or evidence of pending registration, identification of directors and beneficial owners, registered office evidence where requested, and powers of attorney. Foreign corporate shareholders must provide their foreign tax identification details, constitutional documents, proof of existence and authority of representatives; documents may require legalization or apostille and certified Spanish translation. A foreign entity carrying on taxable activities in Spain, making supplies requiring Spanish VAT identification, or acting as a member of a Spanish VAT group must obtain a Spanish NIF. Its Spanish VAT number is the NIF prefixed by ES for intra-EU transactions and VIES identification. Form 036 is also used to register for VAT obligations, intracommunity operator status (ROI/VIES), the Immediate Supply of Information regime where applicable, and other tax censuses. Changes in activity, address, representatives, beneficial ownership or VAT status must be reported to the AEAT within the applicable statutory period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Spanish SL is ordinarily subject to Spanish Corporate Income Tax as a separate legal person; Spain does not provide a general United States-style check-the-box election for an SL. Tax transparency is not generally elective for an SL. Relevant elections or regimes may include tax consolidation for qualifying groups, the special regime for newly created entities, the cash-collection special VAT regime, the Spanish VAT group regime, the REDEME monthly refund regime, and other narrowly defined special regimes. Spanish anti-hybrid mismatch rules implement applicable EU ATAD provisions and can deny deductions, impose inclusion or neutralize duplicate deductions or imported mismatch effects; they do not constitute a general entity-classification election. An SL carrying out electrical-substation installation remains subject to normal entity-level taxation unless a specific statutory regime is validly elected and its conditions are satisfied.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA), the Spanish Value Added Tax system, harmonized with the EU VAT Directive. Certain territories, including the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla, are outside the ordinary Spanish VAT territory and have separate indirect-tax rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for Spanish-established businesses: Spain has no general domestic VAT turnover threshold below which a business may remain unregistered. A Spanish SL commencing an economic activity must register for VAT census purposes before the activity or the relevant taxable transactions begin. The EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold applies principally to specified intra-EU distance sales and certain electronically supplied, telecommunications, broadcasting and television services, not to a general Spanish domestic registration exemption. A non-established supplier may have registration obligations from the first taxable Spanish transaction unless the reverse-charge, OSS or another statutory simplification applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not currently operate a universal real-time pre-clearance system for every domestic invoice. Under the Immediate Supply of Information (SII) regime, mandatory participants generally include businesses with annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million, entities registered in REDEME, VAT groups and entities voluntarily opting in; invoice-record data is transmitted electronically to the AEAT, generally within four calendar days, excluding Saturdays, Sundays and national holidays, with an eight-calendar-day rule for invoices issued by the recipient or a third party. Public-sector contracting invoices are generally required in electronic format and are submitted through the FACe public-sector platform, subject to applicable exemptions and size thresholds. Royal Decree 1007/2023 regulates compliant computer billing systems, including integrity, traceability, preservation, hash or chaining controls and, where the Veri*Factu option is used, transmission of billing records to the AEAT. The implementation timetable has been amended and should be verified against current transitional legislation; the generally stated post-amendment target dates are 1 January 2027 for corporate taxpayers and 1 July 2027 for other covered taxpayers. The broader mandatory B2B electronic-invoicing framework introduced by Law 18/2022 requires implementing regulations and phased commencement; it should not be treated as fully operational for all B2B invoices until the applicable regulations and effective dates have entered into force. Invoices must contain mandatory VAT particulars, including supplier and customer identification, NIF where required, date, sequential number, description, taxable base, rate, amount and reverse-charge or exemption wording where applicable.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from the Spanish VAT territory to a destination outside the EU may be exempt with the right to deduct, provided the goods leave the EU customs territory and the supplier satisfies the documentary and timing requirements. The supplier should retain the export customs declaration and movement reference number, customs confirmation of exit, transport evidence, commercial invoice, packing records, delivery evidence and proof linking the exported goods to the invoice and purchaser. Intra-EU supplies of goods may be exempt with the right to deduct where the customer is VAT-identified in another Member State, the goods are dispatched or transported to that Member State, the supplier reports the transaction correctly and the required transport evidence is maintained. Services supplied to a business established outside Spain may be outside Spanish VAT under the applicable place-of-supply rule, but the result depends on customer status, use and enjoyment rules, and the specific service. Services directly connected with immovable property, including many construction, installation and works contracts relating to a substation site, are generally taxed where the immovable property is located; they are not automatically zero-rated merely because the customer is foreign or payment is received from abroad. A Spanish VAT taxpayer generally recovers input VAT through periodic VAT returns. Non-established businesses may use the EU electronic refund procedure if eligible, or the non-EU refund procedure subject to reciprocity, minimum claim amounts, deadlines and documentary requirements. Fraudulent or unsupported zero-rating can result in assessment of output VAT, late-payment interest, loss or adjustment of input-tax deductions and penalties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration submitted through the Spanish customs electronic system, including the Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Electronic customs confirmation that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, purchaser, goods, value and applicable exemption basis
Packing list and transport documentation, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note or equivalent
Evidence of delivery or receipt at the non-EU destination where relevant
Contract, purchase order and records linking the exported goods to the taxable invoice
For intra-EU supplies rather than exports: customer VAT number, transport evidence and correct EC Sales List reporting
For services: contract, customer business-status evidence, place-of-supply analysis, service-delivery records and evidence supporting any reverse-charge or exemption treatment
Bank or payment records may support the transaction but an inward remittance certificate is not a universal statutory condition for Spanish VAT export exemption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spain has no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for ordinary export proceeds, including no generally applicable 180-day repatriation rule. Export and VAT audits may examine customs exit records, MRN and exit confirmation, transport routes, customer identity, contract terms, place of supply, related-party pricing, payment trails, inventory records and consistency between customs, VAT returns, EC Sales Lists and accounting records. If an exemption or zero-rating claim fails, the AEAT may assess the unpaid VAT retroactively, together with late-payment interest and applicable surcharges. Under the General Tax Law, tax-infringement penalties can commonly range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on concealment, repeated conduct and other aggravating factors; incorrect invoicing, record failures and obstruction may attract separate penalties. Customs infringements may trigger customs debt, administrative fines, seizure or forfeiture under the Union Customs Code and Spanish implementing rules. Deliberate tax fraud may also create criminal exposure where the annual amount defrauded exceeds the applicable criminal threshold, generally EUR 120,000 per tax and tax period, subject to statutory qualifications. Voluntary correction before audit, complete contemporaneous documentation and consistent reporting are material mitigation factors.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating under the European System of Central Banks and ESCB, and the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business for balance-of-payments statistical and foreign-investment reporting; AML/CFT supervision is coordinated by SEPBLAC (Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Spain applies no exchange-control authorization for current-account or capital-account transactions, including profit remittance to non-resident shareholders. Dividends and capital repatriation are unrestricted, but are subject to applicable withholding taxes unless relieved under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or a double-tax treaty, and must be reported through the Banco de España balance-of-payments reporting framework. Payment banks typically require an NIE certificate, a notarised/deceased? Non-resident identity documentation and a current corporate power-of-attorney.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds in Spain. Exporters may retain balances in EUR or freely choose any convertible currency. For statistical purposes, export collection transactions must be reported by the resident company to its financial intermediary or directly to Banco de España in accordance with Circular 4/2004; the filing is due within 15 business days after the month in which the transaction occurs, but no forced repatriation to Spain or fixed conversion percentage is imposed.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Project Milestone Collection Account
Operational Account; Trade Finance Disbursement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium — EU-authorised electronic money institutions and Spanish EMIs operating under Law 21/2011 and EBA passporting can legally open euro settlement accounts and execute cross-border SEPA/MT103 flows, which is feasible for operational liquidity and supplier payments. However, EMIs consistently face restricted ability to issue and handle documentary letters of credit, standby facilities, project guarantees and complex escrow mechanics required for a high-voltage substation installer; for full treasury and trade-finance capability, the SL should maintain a tier-1 commercial bank as primary clearing bank and use an EMI only as a secondary low-value disbursement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish banks normally require at least one authorised director/UBO to appear for an initial branch or remote video-identification interview before account opening is completed. Non-resident directors may complete identity verification using an apostilled passport and a company register certificate, but most tier-1 institutions, particularly for corporate accounts with foreign shareholders, mandate a face-to-face meeting or a bank-approved Smart-ID/VideoKYC process; pure remote opening without an existing banking relationship remains the exception and is generally not available for construction contractors receiving significant inbound capital. Physical presence in Spain is not strictly mandated by statute where an electronic identification procedure accepted by the bank is used, but in practice the bank will require one executive signatory to attend onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial-ownership chain through non-resident intermediate jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current company registry certificate from Spain, apostilled corporate resolutions of every intermediate holding company, complete UBO register declaration modelled on Spanish SL ownership, detailed organisational chart with rationale for interposed entities, audited financial statements of the shareholder chain, and a written explanation of the commercial substance for the structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Positive sanctions/PEP screening on directors, shareholders, suppliers or payment beneficiaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/OFAC sanction screening report, passport and residence proof of all screened persons, PEP declaration with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, notarised declarations of no indirect access by sanctioned parties, and full subcontractor list with ownership verification for each high-risk counterparty.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound equity injection inconsistent with the project contract amount or asset level of the newly formed SL
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital contribution deed, bank statement records of the remitting shareholder, proof of source of wealth (tax returns, audited group accounts, or asset-sale deed), signed shareholder loan/subordination agreements, and the signed EPC or substation installation contract evidencing the commercial requirement for capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disbursement payments to high-risk jurisdictions for imported electrical switchgear or high-voltage components
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed sales and purchase agreements, original commercial invoices pro-forma, bill of lading/air waybill, customs export/import declarations, certificate of origin, export-control licence or EU dual-use certificate where applicable, manufacturer supplier due-diligence file, and evidence that no parallel or undisclosed beneficiary receives project funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders execute a EUR-denominated SWIFT MT103 or a SEPA Credit Transfer into the SL's Spanish capital escrow account, or into a duly declared non-resident capital account, quoting the Banco de España balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment in equity (capital subscription). The bank must be provided with the notarial deed of incorporation, the current statute, the shareholder identity file, and the foreign investment reporting declaration; funds are credited to the operating account only after the full corporate-account compliance check and, where necessary, the Spanish foreign investment statistical form has been filed. For injections exceeding thresholds, additional identification of the ultimate parent and a board resolution clarifying the capital structure are submitted in advance to avoid friction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For milestone payments and weekly progress wires, use SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Instant for domestic euro amounts below EUR 100,000. For imported gas-insulated switchgear and transformer deliveries, issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700/MT707) governed by UCP600, with an advance payment guarantee and performance guarantee issued under URDG758 if required by the principal or supplier, all cleared via tier-1 correspondent banking rails. Payments are settled through TARGET2 for time-critical EUR amounts and through SWIFT FIN for foreign-currency trade settlements; the remittance instruction must carry the underlying import/export commercial invoice reference, customs code, and the applicable balance-of-payments statistical purpose code.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable outright forward (FX forward), executed with the onboarding tier-1 Spanish bank under an ISDA FX Master Agreement or bank standard FX terms
EUR/USD cross-currency swap (FX swap) for liquidity and matching forward purchase of imported equipment
EUR/USD zero-cost collar or purchased currency option to cap procurement cost increases while preserving upside

NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) oriented to exotic-currency procurement exposures, such as USD/CNY for switchgear procured from Chinese suppliers, provided they are used solely for hedging, entered with an authorised credit institution and reported under EMIR/SEPBLAC obligations as applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of fiscal year-end: shareholder approval within 6 months and registry filing within 1 month thereafter; for calendar-year entities by 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry lock ('cierre registral') effective 1 August for calendar-year entities; late-filing fine of EUR 1,200–60,000; no registry filings accepted until deposited; failure to file within 14 months may lead to cancellation of the company's file and eventual strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 25 days, 6 months and 20 days after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities by 25 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Spontaneous late-filing surcharge of 5% (≤3 months delay) up to 20% (>12 months) plus late-payment interest; enforced collection penalty 50% of tax assessed; additional fixed penalty of EUR 200 for late filing without payment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada if, for two consecutive years, it meets at least two of: (i) total assets > EUR 2,850,000; (ii) net annual turnover > EUR 5,700,000; (iii) average workforce > 50 employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Plan General de Contabilidad (Spanish GAAP), adapted to EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; SMEs may apply the PGC de PYMES; groups preparing consolidated accounts use IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SL must maintain an up-to-date statutory register of ultimate beneficial owners and confirm it annually as part of the deposit of annual accounts. Any change in UBO must be filed with the Mercantile Registry within one month; no separate standalone annual UBO filing applies, but the annual accounts deposit includes a confirmation of current beneficial ownership.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro Registro de Administradores)
Record of Annual Accounts (Libro de Cuentas Anuales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 3,000 – 8,000 (approximately USD 3,250 – 8,650), contingent on entity size and transactional complexity
